method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Options now compare realistic aggregation and estimation shortcuts. Separate measured volumes and appearance preserve source-specific trends; supported by primary drain guidance.
Wound separation during removal warrants stopping for assessment. Adding strips or a dressing does not justify continuing removal; the key remains safely scoped.
Current suction volume and actual replacement are more directly relevant to suspected depletion than mouth-care relief, settings or usual home intake. Options are comparable information.
All alternatives now assess relevant urinary data; a post-void bladder check most directly evaluates incomplete emptying suggested by small frequent voids/fullness.
Revised key explicitly pauses inflow while assessing outflow and applying obstruction protocol. This prevents additional distension; antispasmodic or slowed inflow alone does not resolve patency.
Continuous new water-seal bubbling warrants patient/connection assessment. Suction chamber water changes are a plausible chamber-confusion error; prolonged unplanned clamping remains unsafe.

Actual cycling and correct fit establish effective prescribed compression. Oversizing for everyone or routine overnight disconnection undermines therapy. Foundation SATA, with limited higher-order difficulty.
New unilateral tender swelling requires assessment/escalation rather than independent compression escalation, massage or harder exercise. The unrelated other-client stocking distractor is removed.
Incision support helps the client perform prescribed effective coughs. Inspiratory spirometry is a relevant adjunct but does not substitute for secretion clearance.
Closing blinds during a daytime rest can be a reasonable short-term sleep accommodation, while the rationale assumes continuous daytime dimness. Specify sustained removal of day-night cues.
issues: Closing blinds during a daytime rest can be a reasonable short-term sleep accommodation, while the rationale assumes continuous daytime dimness. Specify sustained removal of day-night cues.

options: Provide orientation and preserve sleep where feasible
Remove the clock and calendar to reduce visual clutter
Keep the blinds closed throughout the daytime to maintain a sleep setting
why: Orientation and appropriate sleep support cognitive function.
Clock/calendar cues can support orientation rather than being routine clutter.
Maintaining darkness throughout daytime can disrupt day-night cues; preserve a suitable rhythm.
Accessible hearing and vision aids help interpret the environment.

items.assessment: Inspect/offload local device pressure while maintaining oxygen is a sound patient-specific balance. A covering without correcting tension is now a plausible incomplete workaround.
All alternatives interpret healing. Shrinking dimensions and healthy granulation support progress despite stable mild serous drainage; drainage-only plateau/failure inferences are incorrect.
All alternatives are home-technique demonstrations. Separate output and secure tubing are correct; combining drains and reclosing an expanded suction bulb reveal relevant errors.
Repeated vomiting with increasing distension should pause diet progression for team assessment. Temporary antiemetic response does not establish GI tolerance.

The stem explicitly targets distal neurovascular baseline. Distal motor/sensory and perfusion findings fit; local bruise size and movement pain at the injured joint are broader injury data. This should not be generalized to omitting pain from full neurovascular surveillance.
Approved itch relief and assessment of persistent irritation protect hidden skin. Warm air, objects and poured lotion are relevant unsafe cast-care misconceptions.
